# Loading genus and saving
load("D003093_phyloseq_updated_genus.RData")
ps_genus <- pylsq

load("D003093_phyloseq_updated_species.RData")
ps_species <- pylsq
# Making a dataframe
View(as(sample_data(ps_genus), "data.frame"))

Mean relative abundance for phylum (UC and healthy)

# Using phylum 
ps_phylum <- tax_glom(ps_genus, taxrank = "Phylum")

# Calculating mean abundance for UC patients 
sick_phylum <- psmelt(ps_phylum) %>%
  filter(Disease.MESH.ID == "D003093") %>%
  group_by(Phylum) %>%
  summarise(mean_abundance = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Calculating mean abundance for Healthy patients
healthy_phylum <- psmelt(ps_phylum) %>%
  filter(Disease.MESH.ID == "D006262") %>%
  group_by(Phylum) %>%
  summarise(mean_abundance = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Combining UC and healthy into one dataframe for plotting
phylum_combined <- bind_rows(
  sick_phylum %>% mutate(group = "Ulcerative colitis"),
  healthy_phylum %>% mutate(group = "Healthy")
)
# Plotting
ggplot(phylum_combined, aes(x = group, y = mean_abundance, fill = Phylum)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Mean relative abundance by phylum", x = "", y = "Relative abundance")

Mean relative abundance for genus (UC and healthy)

These are not included in our project, as stacked bar charts do not clearly show which genera are increased or decreased between groups. This is instead addressed in the differential abundance analysis later in this document

# Mean relative abundance of top 20 genera in UC samples
sick_top20_mean <- psmelt(ps_genus) %>%
  filter(Disease.MESH.ID == "D003093") %>%
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  summarise(mean_relative_abundance = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_relative_abundance)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 20)

ggplot(sick_top20_mean, aes(x = "Ulcerative colitis", y = mean_relative_abundance, fill = Genus)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Mean relative abundance of top 20 genera in Ulcerative Colitis", x = "", y = "Relative abundance")

# Mean relative abundance of top 20 genera in healthy controls
healthy_top20_mean <- psmelt(ps_genus) %>%
  filter(Disease.MESH.ID == "D006262") %>%
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  summarise(mean_relative_abundance = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_relative_abundance)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 20)

ggplot(healthy_top20_mean, aes(x = "Healthy controls", y = mean_relative_abundance, fill = Genus)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Mean relative abundance of top 20 genera in healthy controls", x = "", y = "Relative abundance")

Alpha diversity

Shannon and Simpson diversity plots

# Alpha Diversity 
sample_data(ps_genus)$Disease <- ifelse(
  sample_data(ps_genus)$Disease.MESH.ID == "D003093",
  "UC",
  "Healthy"
)

otu <- as.data.frame(t(otu_table(ps_genus)))

# Generating shannon and simpson diversity
alpha <- data.frame(
  SampleID = rownames(otu),
  Shannon = diversity(otu, index = "shannon"),
  Simpson = diversity(otu, index = "simpson"),
  Disease = sample_data(ps_genus)$Disease
)

# Labeling 
alpha$Disease <- factor(
  alpha$Disease,
  levels = c("Healthy", "UC"),
  labels = c("Healthy controls", "Ulcerative colitis")
)

alpha_long <- pivot_longer(
  alpha,
  cols = c("Shannon", "Simpson"),
  names_to = "Measure",
  values_to = "Diversity"
)

# Plotting
ggplot(alpha_long, aes(x = Disease, y = Diversity)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.14, size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ Measure, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Alpha diversity by disease status",
    x = "Disease status",
    y = "Alpha diversity measure"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

# Wilcoxon rank sum test for both Shannon and Simpson
wilcox.test(Shannon ~ Disease, data = alpha)
## 
##  Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction
## 
## data:  Shannon by Disease
## W = 149322, p-value = 0.03217
## alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0
wilcox.test(Simpson ~ Disease, data = alpha)
## 
##  Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction
## 
## data:  Simpson by Disease
## W = 148342, p-value = 0.05178
## alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0

Shannon diversity by contries

# Calculating Shannon diversity and join with metadata
# Samples with missing country are labelled "Unknown"
shannon_country <- estimate_richness(ps_genus, measures = "Shannon") %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample_id") %>%
  inner_join(data.frame(sample_data(ps_genus)) %>% rownames_to_column("sample_id"), by = "sample_id") %>%
  mutate(Country_clean = case_when(
    is.na(Country) | Country == "" ~ "Unknown",
    TRUE ~ Country
  ))
## Warning in estimate_richness(ps_genus, measures = "Shannon"): The data you have provided does not have
## any singletons. This is highly suspicious. Results of richness
## estimates (for example) are probably unreliable, or wrong, if you have already
## trimmed low-abundance taxa from the data.
## 
## We recommended that you find the un-trimmed data and retry.
# Boxplot of Shannon diversity by country
ggplot(shannon_country, aes(x = Country_clean, y = Shannon, fill = Country_clean, color = Country_clean)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.25, outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.35, size = 1.5) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Shannon diversity by country", x = "Country", y = "Shannon diversity") +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Generating Kruskal-Wallis test and pairwise Wilcoxon
kruskal.test(Shannon ~ Country_clean, data = shannon_country)
## 
##  Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test
## 
## data:  Shannon by Country_clean
## Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 185.12, df = 3, p-value < 2.2e-16
pairwise.wilcox.test(shannon_country$Shannon, shannon_country$Country_clean, p.adjust.method = "BH")
## 
##  Pairwise comparisons using Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction 
## 
## data:  shannon_country$Shannon and shannon_country$Country_clean 
## 
##                          Denmark Spain   United States of America
## Spain                    4.7e-06 -       -                       
## United States of America 5.0e-13 < 2e-16 -                       
## Unknown                  < 2e-16 < 2e-16 0.0037                  
## 
## P value adjustment method: BH

Shannon diversity by sex

This plot is not included in the final project

# Calculated Shannon diversity by sex
# Samples with unknown sex are excluded
alpha_sex <- estimate_richness(ps_genus, measures = "Shannon") %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample_id") %>%
  inner_join(data.frame(sample_data(ps_genus)) %>% rownames_to_column("sample_id"), by = "sample_id") %>%
  mutate(sex_group = case_when(
    tolower(trimws(Sex)) %in% c("female", "f") ~ "Female",
    tolower(trimws(Sex)) %in% c("male", "m") ~ "Male",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>%
  filter(!is.na(sex_group))

RDA plot

Making a RDA plot for countries

# CLR-transformation
ps_clr <- transform_sample_counts(ps_genus, function(x) {
  x <- x + 1e-9
  log(x) - mean(log(x))
})

# Extracting CLR-matrix and metadata
clr_mat <- as(otu_table(ps_clr), "matrix") %>% t()

meta_rda <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_genus)) %>%
  mutate(Country_clean = case_when(
    is.na(Country) | Country == "" ~ "Unknown",
    TRUE ~ Country
  )) %>%
  select(Country_clean, Disease.MESH.ID) %>%
  mutate(Disease_group = ifelse(Disease.MESH.ID == "D003093", "Sick (UC)", "Healthy"))

# RDA with countries 
rda_country <- rda(clr_mat ~ Country_clean, data = meta_rda)

anova(rda_country, permutations = 999)
## Permutation test for rda under reduced model
## Permutation: free
## Number of permutations: 999
## 
## Model: rda(formula = clr_mat ~ Country_clean, data = meta_rda)
##            Df Variance      F Pr(>F)    
## Model       3   146.08 40.769  0.001 ***
## Residual 1062  1268.44                  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# Plotting
plot_df <- scores(rda_country, display = "sites") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  bind_cols(meta_rda)

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = RDA1, y = RDA2, color = Country_clean, shape = Disease_group)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "RDA: Microbiome-variation explaned by country",
    color = "Country",
    shape = "Group"
  )

Beta diversity

Bray-Curtis PCoA

# Bray-Curtis PCoA
# No tranformation need here because ps_genus already contains relative abundance data
sample_data(ps_genus)$Disease <- ifelse(
  sample_data(ps_genus)$Disease.MESH.ID == "D003093",
  "UC",
  "Healthy"
)
# Extracting data
sample_data(ps_genus)$Disease <- factor(
  sample_data(ps_genus)$Disease,
  levels = c("Healthy", "UC"),
  labels = c("Healthy controls", "Ulcerative colitis")
)

ord_bray <- ordinate(
  ps_genus,
  method = "PCoA",
  distance = "bray"
)
# Plotting
plot_ordination(
  ps_genus,
  ord_bray,
  type = "samples",
  color = "Disease",
  shape = "Disease"
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(color = Disease), level = 0.95) +
  labs(
    title = "Beta diversity: Bray-Curtis PCoA",
    color = "Disease status",
    shape = "Disease status"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

Jaccard PCoa

# Jaccard PCoA

# Converting to presence/abundance
ps_pa <- transform_sample_counts(
  ps_genus,
  function(x) ifelse(x > 0, 1, 0)
)

ord_jaccard <- ordinate(
  ps_pa,
  method = "PCoA",
  distance = "jaccard"
)
# Plotting
plot_ordination(
  ps_genus,
  ord_jaccard,
  type = "samples",
  color = "Disease",
  shape = "Disease"
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(color = Disease), level = 0.95) +
  labs(
    title = "Beta diversity: Jaccard PCoA",
    color = "Disease status",
    shape = "Disease status"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

Bray-Curtis PERMANOVA

# Bray-Curtis PERMANOVA
sample_df <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_genus))
# Calculating distance by Bray-Curtis
bray_dist <- distance(
  ps_genus,
  method = "bray"
)
# PERMANOVA test
adonis2(
  bray_dist ~ Disease,
  data = sample_df,
  permutations = 999
)
## Permutation test for adonis under reduced model
## Permutation: free
## Number of permutations: 999
## 
## adonis2(formula = bray_dist ~ Disease, data = sample_df, permutations = 999)

## Residual 1064  214.799 0.95761

Differential abundance

Wilcoxon for the 20 best genera

This plot is not included in the final project

# 20 genera based on abundance
wilcox_results <- psmelt(ps_genus) %>%
  filter(Disease.MESH.ID %in% c("D003093", "D006262")) %>%
  mutate(group = ifelse(Disease.MESH.ID == "D003093", "Sick", "Healthy")) %>%
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  summarise(
    # Values
    p_value      = wilcox.test(Abundance ~ group, exact = FALSE)$p.value,
    mean_sick    = mean(Abundance[group == "Sick"]),
    mean_healthy = mean(Abundance[group == "Healthy"]),
    log2_fc      = log2((mean_sick + 1e-6) / (mean_healthy + 1e-6)),
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Benjamini-Hochberg correction
  mutate(q_value = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"))

# Printing results 
wilcox_results %>% arrange(q_value) %>% head(20)

Plot showing which genera that are UC-enriched and Healthy-enriched

# Plot significantly differential abundant genera
# Red = UC-enriched, Blue = Healthy-enriched
wilcox_results %>%
  filter(q_value < 0.05) %>%
  mutate(
    direction = ifelse(log2_fc > 0, "UC-enriched", "Healthy-enriched"),
    Genus = gsub("g__", "", Genus) # Remove "g__" prefix
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Genus, log2_fc), y = log2_fc, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "UC-enriched"      = "#E74C3C",
    "Healthy-enriched" = "#3498DB"
  )) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Differentially abundant genera: UC vs Healthy",
    x     = NULL,
    y     = "Log2 fold change (UC vs Healthy)",
    fill  = NULL
  )
